Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is your idea of a perfect relationship or a perfect marriage?
Answer: An old, experienced man was traveling on a train. In the same compartment, a couple was also traveling. They were in their early 40s. At every station, small or big, the man got down from the train and got something for the woman - Coffee, fruit, chocolate, cookies, etc. Even though the woman denied eating, the man persuaded her to have them. The older man was observing everything, and then he asked the woman about her relationship with the man at one station when he got down searching for something. "Who is he?" He asked. "He is my husband." She answered. "No, he is not your husband." The older man replied. "Why? How can you say that?" She felt a little bothered. "A husband will never do so much. You are telling a lie." The older man smiled. The woman found some affection in his smile and confessed that he was not her husband but her husband's friend who was in love with her. While telling the truth, she blushed, and the happiness on her face was quite visible. This is a story, and I am sure many of you can relate to the statement that a husband will never do so much. Because, at some point in time, marriages lose their charm. The spouses take each other for granted. Getting attention from your partner seems like a dream. That's why I mentioned once that marriages should come with expiry dates. Suppose it has to expire in the next year, then the spouses will do their best to keep the relationship alive if there is a dependency from any side. They will long for the renewal of the marriage at any cost, and for that, they will try to keep their spouse happy and content. Then, no need to have a boyfriend or girlfriend from outside. What a great idea! No? Think about it. We are so conditioned by society that we cannot think of anything beyond the cultural norms. P.S.- this write up is not to glorify the extra marital affair but it talks about an idea of keeping the relationship/marriage lively for a lifetime. By the way, that older man was no one but Osho.😊 Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: I am so alone. I am depressed and lonely and have no friends or significant other. What is wrong with me that makes me so lonely in life?
Answer: For the last two days, I have been feeling like you. I was down in the dumps and had no one to share my feelings with. The more I craved someone with whom I could share my pain freely, the more I felt stifled. "I am no one's priority. No one is concerned about my well-being. There is no one to enquire if I have eaten food or slept well." this thought made me sicker. I hardly ate or drank water. I suffered from insomnia, and during office hours, I dozed off. I felt too fragile even to walk. Out of exasperation, I got furious with a little mistake of my child, yelled at him, and ended up with shedding tears. My sister from far away sensed my despairs and called me to know how I was doing. I enthusiastically exaggerated the taste of chicken soup that I had recently cooked for my child. She couldn't guess what I was going through. This is how a depressed person acts. I felt like consulting a psychiatrist this morning because my depression doesn't seem to fade. Most of the time, I am bright, chirpy, and upbeat, but occasionally, I am clutched by low spirits. And life feels static and pointless. However, in the afternoon, I picked up a storybook by Ruskin Bond and started reading it. After reading a few pages, I felt a little stable. And then, I took the chance to analyze my life, past experiences, desires, and needs. "What is the guarantee that someone (if I find one) will keep me happy?" I asked myself. In the last four years, I have worked very hard to regain my mental peace which I can't ruin by giving someone else the remote control of my life. I have seen people who brutally walked out from my life without giving notice. Come on! I can't make the same mistake. I will work on myself. I am already in love with my aloneness and a bit of loneliness - I will convert it into fulfilling solitude. If I have taken responsibility for my life, I will ensure it is more gratifying. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What should I do if I heard people start gossiping about me?
Answer: Recently, I heard something that made me split my sides. A relative told my mother what other relatives said about me. When I divorced my husband, they spread the rumor that I had an affair and would marry that guy after my divorce. Four years have passed since the separation, and I am still single. However, in these four years, my life became more stable; I gained more freedom, happiness, and peace and established myself as an author. The imaginary guy my relatives saw in their dreams didn't meet me yet, and I am sure he wouldn't ever meet me. Because my taste differs from my relatives, I will definitely not like a guy of their choice and imagination. So I laugh. I enjoy their gossip. And have fun with their rumors. Because I prefer to work on my aspirations rather than pay attention to the blabber of others. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: As a woman, what do some men do that creeps you out?
Answer: Years ago, I was travelling on a train. My co-passengers in my compartment were homely people. There was an old man and his wife, two middle-aged men and a bright young man who was a probationary officer in a bank. Since the journey was nearly 36 hours long, we got along well. The old man liked me for my thoughts and wanted to talk to me more and more. The bank officer grew interested when I shared my opinion on a few topics. The bank officer and I were almost of the same age so we became friends. We shared our Facebook account and he picked up some of my stylish pictures and sent me on WhatsApp commenting something funny but decent. I liked him. He had a great sense of humour. We made fun of everyone on the train through messages and giggled. When we reached our destination, we both exchanged our numbers. At this time, I had grown weary of my monotonous married life though it was just a year old. I really needed someone who could make me laugh. I began to talk to him every day during our office hours. Every day he asked me with care if I had my food on time. I was always smiling and shared the secret of this smile with my husband too. However, slowly, that young man started showing me a different aspect of his personality. He sounded cheap in his talks. His jokes turned obscene and the messages seemed ugly which forced me to block him everywhere. “You need to be careful”, said my husband later. Some men are real creeps. Or I can say, they tend to mistake the inclination that a woman has for them. They walk with a mask on their face which doesn't impress me. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do Indian parents give smartphones to their children at a young age? If so, why?
Answer: I gave a smartphone to my child when he was eight months old. It sounds weird, but I had no choice. He was not good at eating, and I struggled to feed him every day. I have been a working mother and have always been in a rush. All the passersby knew this adamant child as I fed him, making him sit on the wall near the main gate and showing him dogs and cows. I had hired an adult girl as a caretaker who used to feed him in my absence. It was chaos for that girl as well to feed him every time. However, I noticed he could easily take the first few spoons while watching YouTube videos. That eased our task to some extent. So I permanently gave my smartphone to him and bought a new one for myself. He watched videos while having food until the last year. Now, he watches TV or laptop. I have banned the mobile for him. You can blame me for being an irresponsible mother, but I was helpless. He needed some diversion to swallow the morsel; otherwise, he threw it out. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some small things that you miss the most in your life?
Answer: My father adored me when I was a little girl. He was so fond of me that he wanted to see me as soon as he returned from his clinic. He would scoop me into his arms, planting a tender kiss on my forehead, tousling my hair and gently rubbing his chin against mine. At night, he would cradle me and we’d playfully roll in bed, creating moments filled with laughter. This was the love he showered on me during the childhood. “I love her the most” He proudly declared to everyone, expressing his deep affection for me. I cherish those beautiful moments the most in my life. Yesterday, my mother conveyed over the phone that he no longer wishes to travel to Bangalore. He says his body no longer supports extensive journeys; he is now 76. I feel a profound sadness, thinking how things change in our life. He is sacrificing his fondness for his daughter and grandson due to his weakened body. And I am struggling to accept this reality. I miss my father, his love and his fondness. I yearn for those gentle kisses, surprising tickles and daily hugs. I miss him a lot! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What do you think is the easy way that leads us to heaven?
Answer: My grandfather (paternal) was a religious man. He went on several pilgrimages. He never touched non-vegetarian food in his life. He never missed any fast for Ekadashi, which is considered the most auspicious fast in the Hindu religion. He spent his morning and evening offering prayers at the temple that he had only constructed. He donated money and lands to the welfare of society. He built a hospital. He was known for his kindness. He died in his late 80s. I am not sure if he went to heaven, as the concept of hell and heaven doesn't sound promising. However, looking at the crowd that came for his last darshan, I believed that he was God's child. No one in the crowd spoke ill about him. Everyone was just eager to touch his feet and see his face for the last time. Even if the concept of hell and heaven exists, I will not value it much as it comes into existence after death. Instead, I would insist on living like my grandfather, whose demise saddened everyone. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How can I love myself? Are there any tips or a book that can help me start?
Answer: For me, my mental peace is the most important thing in life. I can't compromise on it. I had a boyfriend in the college with whom my inner tranquility was often at stake. Later I was in a marriage where I forgot about my wants and needs. I completely lost my mental health and became insomniac. At present, my emotional well-being is my first priority. I can gracefully exit any relationship where my mental health is at risk, no matter how emotionally involved I am with the person. Because I know how it feels after losing it. So, safeguarding my mental peace is the first sign of loving myself. No book or tip can help you to love yourself. You need to identify your preferences, wants and needs, and then you have to protect them. You need to set boundaries and make sure no one crosses them. Currently, ‘selfless love’ is not in my dictionary. I can only love those who reciprocate the same to me. I make sure I don't chase people blindly. I let people know that they can not take me for granted. It hurts me a lot when I am emotionally involved with someone and that someone neglects me. So, in a relationship, I ensure that I am not hurt. I focus on things that I want in my life. I take care of my health and sleep. This is another version of loving myself. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What should a 21-year-old girl do if she hates household chores?
Answer: She should focus on her career. She should be financially settled to hire a cook and domestic help. Then only she can escape household chores. Otherwise, she has no choice. Though it applies to both genders, it is more applicable to women in our patriarchal society. She is not supposed to sit idle and dictate. A husband is accepted to sit and dictate, but not a wife. Reality! If a woman neither earns money nor does household chores, she is considered useless. And there is nothing wrong with that. To survive, one has to accomplish a few skills. I always had a cook and domestic help to clean the house, but during the COVID, when I was jobless and could not hire a cook, I realized how much cooking skills matter. I learned it in a year. However, my family still considers me dumb when it comes to managing households. Still, I would say — if you are not willing to do household chores, there is nothing wrong with that. It's just a matter of interest. You can utilize your energy and time to do something else and always hire domestic help for your work. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How do you judge yourself?
Answer: I look at myself in the mirror and exclaim, “Oh, I am so young, so beautiful, yet to grow and yet to see the world.” When I go out and feel tempted to eat samosa, noodles, or any other junk food, I remind myself of my age, “Shame on you! How can you think of junk food? Look at your age; your skin is getting dull.” And this certainly helps me avoid junk food. Lol! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: In a relationship, is it okay to act okay even though you are not?
Answer: The relationship is not meant for acting. If you have a true relationship with someone or you desire to lead a long-term relationship with someone, you need to be in your original form. You must remain as raw as you are. I have seen many marriages or relationships that lost their charm too soon. The reason was simple. The couple acted to be okay though they were not okay. They had conflicts and dissatisfaction with each other, which they never expressed. Maybe, they had a fear of losing each other after expressing themselves. They kept quiet for a long which led to monotony, frustration, and hatred. Unknowingly, they created a distance between themselves and could never truly enter each other's space. The relationship felt like a burden. A responsibility to carry for lifelong. If given a chance, one would run away from such a relationship. So I advise you not to act to be okay if you are not okay. Vent out your frustration, speak up and let your partner know what you are going through. Tell them that you need their attention. Also, have the freedom to let them know if you need some space from them to breathe freely. Be what you are. You will then see wonders happening in your relationship. All the best! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some morning habits that can change your day?
Answer: Walking. I go for a stroll in the morning every day. For 10, 20, or 30 minutes as time permits. During this time, while walking, I think of myself. I avoid all negative thoughts and focus on what I want from my life, what I want to do being in this world, and how I want to live. This strengthens my thought process, determination, and willpower. I get to know about the conflicts between my mind and heart. If I can fix them, I try to find a way or leave them to time. I prefer to go with the flow. In my mind, I jot down all those beautiful things I have — my writing ability, my parents, my child, a few fantastic friends, my heartwarming readers, my house, my job, water, the cool breeze blowing my hair, and the ground under my feet. I feel elated, as if I am the most affluent person in the world. This helps me discover my being, the purpose of my existence, and how to work on my aspirations. I want you also to spare 20 minutes every morning for walking when you can spend time only with yourself. At this time, you become your priority. Thank the universe for the things that you have, and show your persistence in getting the things that you want in your life. The universe will definitely grant your wish. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the weirdest thing that happened to you today?
Answer: I was driving to the school to drop off my child this morning when he complimented my bike, mentioning it felt smoother since I had it serviced the previous day. He asked me to drive a little faster, and feeling happy, I increased the speed. However, after 100 meters, I felt a pang in my heart as if an accident was imminent. Immediately, I slowed down and started reciting Gayatri mantra, something I had never done before. I even persuaded my son to join me and with a bit of hesitation, he started chanting as well. As we approached the main road where I needed to take a right turn, another man on a bike with his child joined me to cross the road, but I was behind him. My child and I were still reciting the mantra. Once the man and his child safely crossed the road, I followed suit. However, in the middle of the road, a tractor came speeding towards us and abruptly applied its brakes as it was about to hit us. My heart was filled with fright and uncertainties. I scolded the tractor driver and continued on our way. After dropping my child at school, I had planned to stop for shopping but changed my mind, sensing that the day was not favourable. I decided to return home immediately. The strange part for me was that I had never recited Gayatri mantra before, and later in the evening, I discovered a picture of goddess Gayatri in my phone gallery. I have no idea who sent it to me. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: If you are in a complete and total despair, does it mean you gave up with your life?
Answer: "I've lost all interest in life. I don't want to live anymore. I want to quit." Shared a reader, reaching out with deep agony. "I don't believe it," I replied. "What do you mean? I want to commit suicide," he emphasized. "Nope, I don't think so," I said. "You still want to live, my dear. There's a great interest in life within you," I continued. "How can you say that?" He seemed annoyed with my words. "If you had truly lost interest in life, you would have already taken that step. But you didn't. You came to me, seeking motivation. You still want to live, but you've lost your drive. Something has deeply hurt you, leading to these negative thoughts," I explained. "Hmm..." He calmed down a bit. "You already have a light within you. You just need to recognize it. As you've come to me, finding solace, you are very close to finding it. Awaken your spirit, confront the odds, and overcome the negativity that has engulfed you. Remember, you can!" I continued. "Got it. Thank you! I'll come back to you soon with a new version of myself," he said with a determination, and left. P.S.- At some point in time, we all go through a depressive spell. It's important to open up to someone and share your inner feelings. Depression doesn't mean the end of life; we just need someone to listen, provide emotional support, and guide us toward the right path. So, discover the light within you! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the best random conversation you overheard?
Answer: I was traveling on the metro, and a couple sat beside me. The husband appeared upset and angry, while his wife tried to calm him down. Their little daughter with two ponytails, quite playful and naughty, was unable to get attention from them. So, she was secretly pulling my sleeves and grinning at her mischief. While I was also enjoying her activities, I overheard the couple's conversation. “I can't. I can't listen to them every time.” The husband said in a terse voice. “Why can't you? They are your parents, Rishi.” The wife responded softly. “Soumya, don't you see how they ask for money every time? Just last month, I transferred 5000 Rupees to their account.” He expressed in agitation. “That's okay, Rishi. They need it so they are asking.” “If they need money, why don't they ask Aniket too. He is also earning well. Why me always?” He questioned. “Because they feel more comfortable with you. You are close to their heart.” She explained with a reassuring tone. “But what about us? What about our life? If we keep on giving our money to them, how shall we manage our life?” “We will manage. We have the blessings of our parents. We will never lack anything in life, trust me.” The wife smiled, leaving me genuinely moved. Suddenly their daughter gave me a sharp pinch on my right arm, and I got up from my seat, pulling her cheek softly as my station was about to arrive. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Do you think money can buy anything?
Answer: My father's best friend was in politics. He had a strong personality and owned a lot of property. It wouldn't be wrong if I said he had got swag with everything. The whole family had a luxurious life, and happiness was everywhere until my aunt was diagnosed with blood cancer. The waves of sadness and depression covered the whole family. My uncle spent a lot of money on her treatment which was taking place in one of the best hospitals in Mumbai. He did every possible thing to save her life but couldn't succeed. After six months, my aunt passed away. The children became orphans. Somehow they managed to escape that trauma but lacked guidance, empathy, and love. One of them committed suicide after a few years. Uncle didn't get married again. He became frail and emaciated with time and passed away later. Can money buy anything you want? Money can buy you entertainment but not happiness and peace. It can buy you fun-loving, gregarious friends but no true friendship. It can help you lead a luxurious life, but it wouldn't guarantee you have love and moral support. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Why do women stay in a relationship with men who treat them badly?
Answer: I know many women who are not treated well by their boyfriends or husbands but continue to stay in the relationship. Even when these women are financially independent, they find it difficult to leave an abusive relationship. After a few months of my marriage, I realized that it might not work out. Yet, I continued it for more than seven years. Emotional dependency is the biggest factor that keeps women in loveless relationships. The man they share their life with becomes their world, making it hard to forget and move on. For women who are not financially independent, leaving becomes nearly impossible. “Where would you go? Your parents have already closed their doors to you. So, it's better to adjust with the man who at least provides food and shelter.” is often the advice they receive from people around them. Many women are wise enough to foresee the consequences of separation. In their current relationship, one man mistreats them, yet they maintain a certain level of respect in society. After separation, however, there is a possibility of being mistreated by multiple men. A single woman is often taken for granted, seen merely as an object of pleasure. As a single mother for years, I've experienced firsthand how society struggles to accept me. People either pity my status as if I am a loser or become angry when I stand up for myself. They're more comfortable when I appear needy and vulnerable. This is why many women, even in today's modern world, choose to stay with their partners, whether they're treated like queens or slaves. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Is it okay to act okay when you are not okay?
Answer: Recently, at the onset of a meeting, my Finnish stakeholders asked me how I was doing. “I am not doing well.” I quickly answered without a second thought. They laughed and told me they liked me for being straightforward and honest. They asked me for the reason for not being fine, and I explained them about the heavy workload situation that day. They offered me some support and asked me to avoid doing a few tasks for the day as they were not mandatory. I was relieved. However, it doesn't work with all the people we meet. Some people love to hear that we are not okay. For them, our not being okay is a feel-good medicine. So, we need to be careful. The straightforwardness that I showcased in front of my stakeholders doesn't work everywhere. Therefore, you need to act even you are not okay. A friend used to tell me how she presented herself as completely fine in front of her enemies who waited for her downfall, even though she was going through very tough times. The world around us consists of both good and bad people. Surviving with them is not an easy job. We must learn to handle them to protect ourselves from negativity. Hope you like this practical advice. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: If you could write a love letter to any food or drink, what would you choose, and what would you say?
Answer: Dear Fruits, I want to express my gratitude and affection to you through this letter. I want to tell you how much I feel for you. I love to see you in the fruit basket that I place on my dining table. I fall for you for being so colorful when I open my fridge. My days are incomplete without you. I become cranky when I don't savour you. You are so caring by nature. When I suffer from acid reflux, you are the one who takes the utmost care of me. You have already healed me to some extent. My body feels at its best when I add you to my meals. I am thankful to nature for gifting you to us. If I have nothing to eat or feel too lazy to cook, or I need to carry some snacks while going out for a few hours, I immediately turn towards you. You are my savior - so easily available to me. I adore you, really! And yes, I miss you when you are not around or become unreachable sometimes due to high cost. Love you for being always there for me. And I recommend everyone to fall in love with you. You are much better than Mr. Noodles and his wife Mrs Pasta or Mr. Samosa and his children Chaat-Pakoda. You are irreplaceable! Yours Anshu. P.S.- I love to click pictures of my fruit bowls. The attached pic is from my mobile camera.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is something a child said that left you flabbergasted?
Answer: My six-year-old boy is amiable by nature. He is popular in his class and made many friends in the school. Being a single mother, I have always been worried about his upbringing. My ex-husband unfortunately never tries to meet him. I always wondered how he would react upon being asked about his father. I wondered if he would be able to manage the question mark on the whereabouts of his father. But yesterday, something happened that obliterated all my worries. Here is the conversation with him after coming from school yesterday: "You know, Mumma, I was annoyed today with Nehan." He talked about his best friend. "Why so? What did he do?" "He was asking me again and again - where is your daddy?" He explained. My heart thumped with fright after hearing this. "What did you say then, Sweetie?" I asked, concealing my nervousness. "I told him that my daddy is the king of Russia. So he is in Russia," he said and giggled. "What did then Nehan say?" I asked in disbelief. "What will he say? He stood open-mouthed." He laughed again. And then, we both laughed together. Later, he told me that Nehan stopped asking about daddy. I felt happy to learn that this tiny creature is growing smart. He has learned to handle difficult situations humorously. And more than this, he has learned to accept life. What else does a single mother desire? Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the most important thing in a relationship?
Answer: Recently, over coffee, I met a friend who is certainly a wise man. We talked about many things, such as career, marriage, life, the quality of coffee, and simultaneously, the quality of the relationship. The relationship sustains as long as its quality persists. Humans are designed to feel loved, wanted, and heard. They are in desperate need of — love, affection, touch, and nudges. You feel left out if your partner is insensitive and least bothered about your needs. The relationship becomes cold, and you feel low. When I was in a loveless marriage for years, I felt my confidence was declining. Initially, I tried making my partner happy, I performed stupid activities to get his attention, but gradually, I gave up. I realized one-sided efforts are futile. But this caused pain. I was often hurt and demotivated. I read somewhere a child grows more confident when he is frequently hugged, loved, and touched by his parents. Otherwise, he grows suppressed. And I was that suppressed wife. Be it a man or woman — everyone is in the same need. They wish to be recognized for love. They want their partners to reward them with hugs, touch, and love because they are designed to feel emotions. The relationship is dead if there is no emotional touch. This touch has to be both mental and physical. Your body and soul — both should be equally touched for a successful relationship. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: Whats the greatest act of love you've received?
Answer: When I went to live in a hostel, I was miserable. This was the first time I stayed away from my parents. I was always on edge and wept alone for hours. I didn't know how to wash clothes or even how to oil my hair. These two tasks seemed too difficult to me. There was a maid in my hostel. I guess she was in her late 50s. Once at night, I soaked my clothes in water mixed with detergent powder thinking of washing them the next morning. I stayed alone in my room. At midnight, I developed severe pain in my right arm. I was not able to move my hand. Out of pain, I was crying. This lady slept just outside my room. She knocked on my door as soon as she heard me crying. After knowing the matter, she ran into the kitchen, heated mustard oil and applied it gently on my arms. After 30 minutes of massage, I felt better and drifted into deep sleep keeping my head in her lap. In the morning, she washed all my clothes. Since that day, she became my second mother. She was always affectionate to me. She washed my clothes without others knowing. I paid money for this but still, it was not allowed in the hostel. She secretly came to my room every Saturday night to apply oil to my hair. I never ate the snacks sent by my mother without sharing them with her. Sometimes, I even gave my pocket money to her which she did not want to take. During my exams, before leaving for the examination hall, I touched her feet secretly as I didn't want anyone to know about this relationship. I did not have the confidence to do it publically. I still miss her. I wish I could see her once again. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What are some little things you can do that greatly boost your confidence?
Answer: After living a miserable life for years, this is how I boosted my confidence to lead a graceful life. Hope, this helps you too. P. S. - I have written a book based on my life - experiences which is available on Amazon and Flipkart. You can read it to look at things from a different perspective and gain confidence in things that you do. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is love to you? What do you think loving someone means?
Answer: “Will you be in my life forever?" she asked. “Yes, love, I want to live with you forever", he answered, gathering her in his arms. "I will end up in a mental hospital if you ever leave me." She confessed while tears rolled down her cheeks. "Then, we both will be in a mental hospital." He said firmly. She looked straight into his eyes and then melted back into his arms. The sheet, the pillows, and the subdued light in the room witnessed two souls becoming one. Loving someone means accompanying them throughout the journey of life. "I want to explore the world. Though I love you, I can't give you commitment because of my aspirations." She said. "Commitment? Unfortunately, this word doesn't exist in my dictionary. I am not willing to cage you. I want you to soar high and touch the sky - with or without me. I love and will love you no matter where you go." He said, smiling. Loving someone means giving them absolute freedom to grow. Buddha said, "You don't pluck a flower if you love it." "I don't want ever to become a trouble or burden for you, but a home where you come to feel relaxed. I wish to be your calm." She said. And upon hearing this, he kissed her neck gently and fondled her from the back. Loving someone means giving them peace. Love is an unselfish act by which you want to achieve only one thing - your lover's happiness. You become a giver - A giver who doesn't expect anything in return. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is life without a husband?
Answer: When my child was born, my husband was in a different city for two years. At that time, no work-from-home was given. I was handling everything all alone with the help of a nanny at home—office, home, and baby. I had many sleepless nights and dozed off in the office while working. I was busy on weekends, taking my mother-in-law to hospitals for regular checkups. I stepped out of my marriage when my child was three. Since then, It has been tough managing everything single-handedly. All these years, I have been too occupied with my daily chores. I have no time for myself. I am responsible for each and everything that happens in my life. I have no one to blame and claim. No matter how sick I am, I must work and care for my child. I have to cook, clean, teach, fulfill his demands, and the list goes on and on. Sometimes, I feel how difficult everything is when I drive alone late at night for any emergency. I have no one to ask me to sit at home and do the work on my behalf. So, life without a husband is challenging. Many of my female readers wish to know about life after divorce. I say - Go for divorce only if you have the zeal to survive and prove your worth; otherwise, you will break. You will have lots of mental peace after separation, but there will be other adversities, too, and you will need to learn how to tackle them. Life will be stable once you learn this skill and gain confidence. But it takes time. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: When will life get easier?
Answer: I was living in a dilemma. I knew I was not happy in my marriage but I had no guts to come out of it. I was scared of living alone. I had no confidence to lead a life, taking all the responsibilities of a child on my own. On top of that, I was demoralised by a statement that I would come on road if I break the marriage. I was really scared. However, the constant pain of the toxic relationship was not letting me live either. I had developed a thin border between living in a loveless marriage and living life on my own. The borderline had to be broken and to do so, it needed a huge amount of bravery that I didn't have. With time, I realised I would die this side as well as that side. Then why not to take risk and see what is there that side of border. This curiosity gave me courage to break the line. And after breaking it, life got easier, at least it met my expectations. How does life get easier? When you overcome your dilemma, life becomes easier. When you take risk and be ready to face the consequences, you get a sense of winning. You feel at ease. Being in the dilemma makes you handicapped as you are unable to take an action and try to compromise with all the tantrums that life throws on you. If you make efforts to lessen the complications of life, it becomes easier. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What is the one thing you will never do again?
Answer: I tried changing people's minds regarding sex — both online and offline. According to ordinary people, there is no life without sex. A man or woman will get into depression without it. I have been without sex for many years now. I never felt depressed. I never felt a requirement for it. I have been asked how I control my sexual desires. This question amazes me to the hilt. For common people, having a male friend means having sex with him. I have been asked if I lost my virginity to my boyfriend during my college days. People really don't know the woman who resides in my body. For this woman, physical and mental intimacy are two different things. Physical intimacy is often lustful in today's world. Everyone is running for it. They are in a hurry to get it. However, my perspective on physical intimacy is different. Physical intimacy comes into existence when love reaches its peak — selfless love! And to know how selfless and unconditional love is, you must spend years together. But nobody is ready to wait. I have written about it in my book and many times on Quora, but I couldn't find any change in people's mindsets. I will never tell people again how sacred and divine sex can be. And every relationship with the opposite gender doesn't lead to sex, at least in my life. If I ever look for a partner, I will ensure that he first touches my soul and then, my body. And I know this is really hard to find someone like this in today's world. That's why I decided to remain single all my life. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What is the most frustrating feeling?
Answer: Recently I read the novel, "The stationary shop of Tehran," where a couple fell in love and desperately wanted to live life together. But the boy's mother didn't like this relationship, just out of her ego, and secretly created misunderstandings between the couple, which separated them forever. In the evening of their life, the couple meets again. The man reveals to the woman that only his mother was responsible for their separation. He wishes that his mother wouldn't have been this cruel. Once, a colleague told me her parents didn't like her boyfriend and tried her best to break the relationship. However, she could overcome her parents' stubbornness and marry her boyfriend. Now, she is living happily, and her boyfriend-now-husband takes care of her parents as well. She, too, wished that her parents could support her. When I remember my days with my ex-in-laws, my heart sinks with disappointment. They, too, tried hard to create differences between my ex-husband and me. What is the most frustrating feeling? When we get to know that our loved ones only don't like our happiness. Due to their possessiveness, insecurity, and trust issues, they tend to spoil our life. Instead of guiding us to save the relationship, they instigate us to break it. P.S. Dear teenagers, don't get misguided by this write-up. Sometimes, our parents are right too. They try to save us from being trapped in a relationship with the wrong person. So think wisely. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: What is the difference between settling for things and accepting the way things are?
Answer: I grew up observing my maternal grandmother, who has been very calm all her life. My grandfather has been an angry, dominating husband who has learned only to rule. During my childhood, I saw him losing his temper and shouting at my granny. But she always stayed calm and serene. She never raised her voice and was always ready to serve him. Why? Because she accepted the circumstances, she wholeheartedly accepted an angry man as her husband. And then, she was at peace. She had no complaints, no regrets, and no sadness. She only focused on her duties. However, I was resentful, cranky, and sick when I was in a marriage. I was unhappy and full of complaints. At times, I was suicidal too. Because I had no guts to come out of this toxic marriage, I was trying to settle with my circumstances, which was causing a lot of pain to me. I had lost my peace. Settling with the situation is often against one's wish - a compromise, whereas accepting the situation shows one's willingness to adjust and adapt to the circumstances. I hope this clarifies the difference. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: How can any person speak English in one day?
Answer: I come across people who consider English a big deal and struggle to get hold of it. I would like to tell those people that English is just a language. Please don't make a fuss. Be it any language, it comes to us with practice. I tried to learn Kannada but never succeeded. The reason was simple. I never had people with whom I could practice. I had no one to correct my grammar. And gradually, I lost my interest too. For the last six years, I have always had an adult girl to look after my child. Most of them had just passed the primary school, but staying with us, they became fluent in English within a year. My ex-husband, my child and I always spoke in English. Listening to us, they learnt. Also, they had developed a sheer desire to speak English. They requested me to correct them if they made a mistake while speaking. This improved their language and the guests in my house admired them. So I would say — you can not speak a language in one day but yes, with practice and in the right environment, you can definitely learn it in a short span of time. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Have you ever had a weird dream that you could never forget and after so many years it still haunts you when you remember it?
Answer: During my teenage, I often used to see snakes in my dreams. They were in bulk. All in black color, moving simply near my feet. They didn't hurt me, but I used to be very afraid, shivering and sweating. I woke up from sleep with fear. And this dream came often. I told my mother about it. She discussed this with our temple priest, who gave me a stone and instructed me to wash it with milk and put it in a black string. And then, I had to tie it to my bed. I followed the instructions. And the frequency of dreams surprisingly reduced. And slowly, it disappeared from my life. However, I am still terrified of snakes. I can't see them in the zoo, in movies, in photos, or even cartoons. And the thought of those dreams still haunts me. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Why do I feel worthless most of the time?
Answer: You feel worthless because: Nowadays, I am so busy with my job, studies, child, and household work that I don't have time to think of anything extra. I am committed to achieving my goals with unwavering focus. Along the way, I may stumble, and all my efforts might be in vain but I am not dwelling on that. However, back in 2016 or 2017, it was not like this. I felt worthless all the time. I was emotionally unstable, constantly longing for affirmation, acceptance, and approval from others. This made me feel vulnerable, needy, and ultimately worthless. But when I started working on myself, things drastically changed. My determination and enthusiasm for improvement attracted like-minded people who helped me grow and guided me when needed. In my bullet points, I used “haven't yet” in each reason for feeling worthless. This means you still have time, opportunity, and potential to start doing things that will give you confidence. So, get up. Open your diary and jot down the things you should do or achieve daily. Follow them with full commitment. Many people, like myself, find that taking small steps towards self-improvement can gradually change how we perceive our worth. Wish you all the best! Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Have you ever had a conversation with a stranger, what did you talk about?
Answer: As I entered the bustling schoolyard, the laughter and chatter of children filled the air. I had just arrived to pick up my son. Out of the crowd, a young boy with curly hair and cute nose approached me. “Aunty! Aunty! Your son beat me today.” he complained. “Oh! I am sorry, baby.” I apologised. “Look at these scratches, he did this to me.” He showed me some scratches on his arms, leaving me in disbelief. “Oops! I am so sorry, darling. Why did he beat you?” I asked, while I lowered myself to his level and hugged him. “I swear, Aunty, I didn't do anything. I just took his new pencil box and he got angry.” He explained. “A new pencil box? But he didn't get any new pencil box, Sweetheart.” “He got, he got! A golden colour one!” He screamed. I wondered. I made a strong effort to recall if I ever bought my son a golden colour pencil box. “Look, he is there - your son is there”. He suddenly yelled pointing out to a child. “Whoa! He is not my son, Sweetheart.” “Look, that's my son.” I luckily saw my child running with his friends in the playground. “Ohh! Is Shourya not your son?” He rolled his eyes in exasperation. “No.” “But Shourya said you are his mother before I came to you.” “Umm! Shourya was just playing a little trick on you, Sweetheart.” “Umm, ok” the little stranger nodded and walked away. A warm smile spread across my face. I hope, it made you smile too. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Can you write some random moments here?
Answer: It was 12:45 am. I was not getting sleep. The characters of the book, 'The stationary shop of Tehran,' were secretly calling me. My six years old had drifted into a deep sleep. However, he was still holding me tightly. I meticulously removed his hand from my bosom and shifted to another bedroom. Looking at the book lying on the bed, I felt relieved. The serenity of nights always pushes me to read and write more. So I picked up the book without wasting a minute and started reading it. While engrossed in reading, I felt a creature standing beside the bed. My heart pounded. I was afraid to take my eyes off the book. "Mumma, why did you come here?" I heard. I was surprised to see my moppet at this time. "Didn't you sleep, Jani? How come you here?" I asked. "I had slept but woke up because you were not there. I don't feel good without you. What are you doing here?" "I am reading, Shona baby." "Okay, then you read. I will sleep here only." He lay down in my lap, covering himself with his baby blanket. Before closing his eyes, he kissed me and smiled once. I was smitten with this gesture. And while I stroked his hair, he fell asleep again. This little munchkin is so close to my heart. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Question: Is there something you realized you wrongly blamed your parents for?
Answer: I was immensely hurt when my mother separated me from my dad by sending me to my Aunt's house for schooling. I was six and hated studying. In my small hometown, I ran away from school. Or I troubled the teachers. The tutors at home have been frequently changed because either they could not sustain with me or I couldn't. I broke their sticks and cried non-stop. My father adored me, so he hated to see me in tears. He made up his mind to have me as illiterate and asked my mother not to pester me to study. However, my mom was another adamant woman who did not want to give up so soon on me. So she secretly planned to send me to my Aunt's house, which was in a different city. I got admission to a convent school where the rules were too strict. I had no way to run away from school. Initially, I hated it. I badly missed my father and sobbed in his arms whenever he came to meet me. It was a tough time for both of us. My mother was denounced for being a stone-hearted woman. However, this was a turning point in my life. There worked some magic, and I grew inquisitive and fascinated by books. Getting the first rank in the class became my goal ever since. So my mother's efforts proved to be a blessing in disguise. Now, I am grateful to her for taking such harsh steps during my childhood. Question: As an introvert, why do I enjoy socializing with people?
Answer: I had always wondered, thinking about what sort of an introvert I was. I have been a reserved person and abstain from opening up. I like to remain in my own circle, which I hate to be invaded. I don't mind calling myself as choosy or fussy when it comes to select people for a company. I'm not particularly eager to mingle with everyone. However, on the other hand, I love people. Many of my friends call me a people's person, as I enjoy socializing. I like to spend time with them hearing their stories. At times, my curiosity is at its peak. I want to learn more about life, people and their thought process, which pushes me to socialize. The world then sees an entirely different Anshu, who is talkative, sympathetic, and more social. I believe that being an introvert or extrovert doesn't matter to socializing with people. As Aristotle said, man is a social animal. Socializing is in our genes. The only difference between an introvert and an extrovert is that an introvert might take more time to mingle with others or be more selective in choosing people for a company. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
